item: exclusive_window pauses the scheduler and counts itself inside its try, so an interrupt cannot leave the hold or the depth up (R171)
status: shipped (local, applies on a tree that has Q's follow-on 77b4b9c88; Q's scan test owes this entry)
refs: R171; hunk pair from Q, adapted to the overlapping-windows count
summary: exclusive_window held the scheduler (hold_exclusive, then stop) BEFORE its try and then counted itself (depth, flag, paused) before the try too, so a Ctrl-C landing between the pause and the try (scripts/run_scale_bench.py is the CLI that reaches it on a main thread) left collection held for good and the depth up for good. The pause and the count are now inside the try; a counted flag is set in the same step as the depth, so the finally lowers the depth only for a window that raised it, and a nested window that never counted gives nothing back. Stated limit: an interrupt before the pause has reported leaves was_paused False, so the finally releases the hold and does not start the loop (it cannot tell whether the stop happened); the worst case is a scheduler neither held nor running, which the Start button puts right. After the pause has reported, the resume is exact (the paused flag is set before the count). Q wrote the pair against the single-window version; this one is adapted to the count and carries two more tests (a nested window interrupted before it counted leaves the outer one standing; one that never counted does not give the scheduler back a second time when the outer one left first). Five tests; two are red without the code, and three mutants (lower the depth for an uncounted window, resume for it, skip the release of an uncounted first window) each fail one.
